title: When is the Thai holy day, and is it the real full moon?

steps.note: Thai holy days from the Suriyayatra arithmetic, two rule changes found from the rows; all 49 of Thai PBS's 2026 match; full-moon day is the sky's full moon in 193 of 446 (43.3%), 242 early, 11 late
Quill's no caught a sentence wider than the test; the Wikipedia table adds a leap day in 2024 that the build adds in 2030

lean.mjs answers the cloud: the full moon comes on average 24.9 h after waxing 15 begins, 0.9 h after the holy day ends, so the pile is centred on the day's last midnight; the mean moon alone never comes before the day (207 on, 239 after). The new moon sits 6.6 h into day 1 (on waxing 1 275 times, on the dark-moon day 130). My sawtooth guess was not the reason. A histogram on the face; 4 new checks, all pass.

Quill's finish no fixed: the windows are the 24 that start on the hour, the sawtooth is measured (+8.8 h a normal year, -15.2 a leap-day year, -2.5 a leap-month year, the arithmetic to within 0.05 h), and every number in the README section is a check but three, which it names. 10 new checks in all.
Correction to the step above: 9 new checks, not 10 (4, then 4, then 1). I counted from memory instead of the file.

count.mjs: the holy days of 2013 and 2014 against a 2014 Royal Institute journal count (24 and 34 of 52 ahead of the Moon's true tithi). A second road to the sky (Meeus ch. 25 and 47) meets the first at 54 new and full moons to 0.0134 degrees. Read as each day begins, mine are 22 of 50 and 36 of 49, never behind; their 52 is a total I can't make (49 here and on Kapook's list). Plan changed at the build door's quarter phases: the paper's Thai sentence counts tithis, so this does too. Six new checks.

Quill's seam closed: count.mjs's road check now uses the same 54 moons as test.mjs (it had dropped the ones outside 2013-2014); both print 0.0134 degrees. Quill read the files but could not run them; I ran both after the change, all passed.

Asahna Bucha 2005 settled: a holiday notice filed with the Thai stock exchange (Dec 2004), Pattaya Mail (15-21 Jul 2005) and MGR Online (20 Jul 2005) all say Thursday 21 July, this build's day. Thai Wikipedia's table said 21 July too, until revision 7771106 (8 Aug 2018) made it the 20th and shifted eight cells of the 2020s row. Revision 8306984 (21 May 2019) then added one day to all twelve 2020s cells. That fixed 2020-23 and 2030-31 and made 2024-29 a day late, which is the table's late stretch this build had found. Seven new checks; the face's footer says it. Quill's two loose ends fixed: the first-row claim narrowed to the one cell read, and the provincial page linked.
